questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Culture, cost of living, weather

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The difficulty varied. Often it required active search rather than by default.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The International Office provided assistance and my professors and other students also reached out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: In comparison with my home university the information was late and limited. I was not too stressed about it but I can imagine that others would be so.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was ok but it's always difficult when you don't know how everyday life will be. I would have considered other neighborhoods if I had known how it would turn out beforehand. I'm glad I prioritized the social and logistic pros of Salerno over the university at Fisciano.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Depending on your studies it can be annoying when the public transport is unreliable but it's not a big deal.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It wasn't the nicest but housing was cheap compared to bigger cities and not very difficult to find

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: With help from locals I new before arriving it was fine but it would have been rather difficult on my own

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Through some links you could find info about the course, through others the timetable, through others the professor

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Both official and unofficial that collectively made it possible

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress as most can be figured out when you're there

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It wasn't the too complicated and very interesting

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: No breaks, less attention and more disturbment among students in class, same enthusiasm and engagement with students from the professors

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Italian Linguistics
Cultural Anthropology and Etnography
Cultural Geography

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked all of them, though as a non native speaker Italian Linguistics was very difficult to follow

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It was difficult to do sports for free, especially since even the terrain was bad for running

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Some transportation was very cheap and other rather expensive. Some food was very cheap but supermarket prices were similar to Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything is overcomplicated in Italy, luckily I got to join training with a local football team in Salerno

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds though I thought the campus lacked social areas outside the classrooms

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think my situation was different as a student of Italian language and culture

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Ice cream at Nettuno and Gusto 17, lunch/dinner at Pizza Portafoglio and Ni Burti. Watch Salernitana, visit the market by the old stadium, enjoy the city center and the coast, visit Vietri Sul Mare instead of Amalfi

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Some things were easy, others pretty difficult

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them, most are curious and many have an ok english

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Lack of cue culture by the bus, inefficient approches to many things

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The mediteranian lifestyle, the generel hospitality and the fan culture at football games

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the region with a lot of nature, city life, culture and history to see, find housing in Salerno, use your own interests as a guideline for activities, there are many ways to use your time

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The warm clothes is only necessary for first week of March so save space on to many long sleeves

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: There are severel. Language, understanding cultures and reviewing your own, amazing experiences, many new relations

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having a girlfriend at home

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
